claims.text: ARF: aspirin for everyone with arthritis and/or mild carditis (controls fever and pain).
claims.quote: Aspirin controls fever and pain and should be given to all patients with arthritis and/or mild carditis.

claims.text: No improvement after 24–48 h of high-dose aspirin: reconsider the diagnosis.
claims.quote: If no improvement is seen after 24 to 48 hours of high-dose aspirin therapy, the diagnosis of ARF should be reconsidered.

claims.text: Children/adolescents: most experts give 15–25 mg/kg PO 4×/day (max 4–6 g/day) for 2–4 wk, then taper over another 4 wk.
claims.quote: Most experts would give children and adolescents 15 to 25 mg/kg orally 4 times a day (to a maximum daily dose of 4 to 6 g) for 2 to 4 weeks and then taper the dose over another 4 weeks.

claims.text: Salicylate toxicity (tinnitus, headache, hyperpnea) limits therapy and may not appear until after 1 wk;
claims.quote: Salicylate toxicity is the limiting factor to aspirin therapy and is manifested by tinnitus, headache, or hyperpnea; it may not appear until after 1 week of therapy.

claims.text: salicylate levels are measured only to manage toxicity.
claims.quote: Salicylate levels are measured only to manage toxicity.

claims.text: Precautions: avoid in severe renal failure (GFR < 10 mL/min)
claims.quote: Avoid aspirin in patients with severe renal failure (glomerular filtration rate less than 10 mL/minute).
Avoid aspirin in patients with severe hepatic insufficiency.
